text: The bay door screams upward an inch. Metal shrieks.
Ray's eyes lock on yours. They found us, he mouths.
Dana shoves you toward the forklift. "Move the water pallets. Now."
Marcus jumps into the cab. The engine coughs, catches, roars.
You stack three pallets against the door. Each slab freezing heavy.
Headlights pulse through the gap. Four silhouettes wait in the dark.
Ray nods at the beam. "They dug down while the storm buried us."
"Heard them in the lot before the snow," Ray says. "A plow truck."
"Plan to empty the warehouse while the roads are closed."
Dana's radio crackles. "Marcus, hold the line. I'm checking the cameras."
The monitor flickers. Camera six still loops the empty nest.
Then the keypad by the bay door beeps. Once. Twice. Three times.
Someone is entering the code from outside.
Dana freezes. "My alarm code. The page is missing from Ray's notebook."
Ray swears he never took it out. His voice raw. "I didn't."
The beeping stops. A green light flashes on the panel.
The bay door shudders. The pallets groan. Ice cracks under the weight.
Marcus revs the forklift. He rams the barricade tighter. "Hold!"
The door rises another foot. Cold wind slams into your face.
A voice booms from the gap. "Open up. We know you're in there."
Ray lunges forward, zip ties straining. "Crawlspace. Behind the racking."
Dana grabs his shoulder. "Not yet. We need the roof hatch key."
The wall clock clicks three in the morning. Generator dead for hours.
Your flashlight beam catches a chain hanging from the plow truck's hitch.
Marcus sees it too. "If we hook that chain to the forklift..."
The pallets start sliding. The barricade gives way inch by inch.
Ray stares at the widening gap. "They're coming through."
Dana's hand finds yours. "Whatever happens, we stay together."
The door crashes fully open. Headlights blind you.
